sdlc_local_verdict: positive (matches this container's own driver classification: primary_metric_win, held_out.structural_similarity 0.3417 -> 0.37006)

cross_session_synthesis.claim: This session's c4 numerically replicates continuous-openui-20260801-c4-results (open PR #1248, 'steps lever mpr win', branch claude/great-dirac-1lxqx7) to 4+ decimal places on both arms. A THIRD parallel session running the SAME nominal cycle 4 recipe (open PR #1247, branch claude/great-dirac-csq5iq, 'held-out regression') measured c4-control.held_out.structural_similarity = 0.38248 and a NEGATIVE primary delta of -0.0124 -- the opposite sign.
cross_session_synthesis.root_cause_hypothesis: c4-control only completed 1 of 5 held_out documents within the 3-minute wall cap in both this session and PR #1248 (completed_document_n=1), while PR #1247's control run apparently completed more documents before the same wall cap (its control held_out.structural_similarity of 0.38248 differs from the 1-document values seen here and in #1248). c4-steps (doubled training steps) reliably completes all 5/5 held_out documents in every session observed so far (structural_similarity pinned at 0.37006 across this session and #1248). The steps lever's apparent effect on held_out.structural_similarity is confounded with, and may be entirely explained by, how many held_out documents the CONTROL arm happens to finish before the shared 3-minute wall -- a real-machine-speed race, not a property of the steps lever itself.
cross_session_synthesis.evidence_for_confound: held_out latency_ms_p50 for control clusters near 19.1-19.5s across all three sessions (0.3417@19067.94ms here-matching-#1248, 0.3417@19458.37ms this session, 0.38248@19385.10ms in #1247) -- consistent with a single slow first document dominating a small/partial completed sample, so the *value* of structural_similarity swings with *which* document(s) happened to finish, not with a stable multi-document average.
cross_session_synthesis.recommendation: Do not credit the steps lever with the held_out.structural_similarity delta until the harness either (a) requires held_out.completed_document_n == n on both arms before comparing structural_similarity as a primary endpoint, or (b) raises the promotion-cycle wall cap enough that control reliably completes the full held_out suite. This is a measurement-integrity gap in the model_build/eval harness family (partial-suite averaging under a wall-clock race), not a validated positive lever result -- flagging for improve-openui-harnesses rather than treating as ship-relevant evidence.

conclusion: This container's own driver classified c4 positive on held_out.structural_similarity, exactly reproducing PR #1248's numbers. But a third open PR (#1247) measured the opposite sign on the same nominal cycle with a fuller control-arm completion. Given all three sessions' control arms show high variance tied to partial held_out completion under the wall cap, this cycle's 'positive' result is treated as UNRELIABLE pending a harness fix, not as grounds for a new stacked layer -- see cross_session_synthesis above.
